In Q1 2026, citation reliability was the single most prominent complaint in customer feedback, with users reporting incorrect source file references, missing page numbers, empty citations, and broken links [NL-010#NL-010-S01]. A deep-dive of 210 accuracy tickets showed the breakdown as 42% incorrect file links, 28% missing page numbers, 18% empty citations, and 12% broken links [NL-010#NL-010-S05]. This caused severe operational issues, such as BrightPath Healthcare pausing its clinical pilot and financial advisors losing confidence in the platform [NL-010#NL-010-S05].

In Q2 2026, following the April 2026 product release, user complaints regarding incorrect or missing citations dropped significantly and trust improved, leading BrightPath Healthcare to restart its clinical pilot [NL-011#NL-011-S03]. Support tickets related to citation issues declined steadily throughout Q2, with citation accuracy tickets falling from 88 in March to 42 in April, 31 in May, and 24 in June [NL-011#NL-011-S05]. The overall NPS rose to 44 (up from 41 in Q1), driven by the successful April update that addressed these critical citation issues [NL-011#NL-011-S01].

However, the trend shows the problem was not fully eliminated. Citation tickets did not drop to zero; the remaining tickets in May and June are almost entirely linked to scanned, image-only PDFs, and there is a minor lag in citation indexing during peak business hours [NL-011#NL-011-S05]. The lack of advanced OCR processing remains a significant pain point, particularly for healthcare and manufacturing customers with legacy scanned manuals [NL-016#NL-016-S04].
